conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Mr. James, I’m Dr. Patel. You were brought in after being found slumped over. You’re at the hospital now. How are you feeling?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m okay… just tired. What time is it? I need to go.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s early evening. We’re concerned because your blood pressure was low when you arrived, and you were very drowsy. You’ve had some fluids, and your pressure has improved.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yeah, I drink sometimes. But I’m fine now. I don’t need to stay.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We know you’ve had a lot of alcohol recently—your level was high. You also have COPD, and your oxygen was low. You needed 4 liters of oxygen at one point.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I know I have breathing problems. But I’ve been through this before. I’ll rest when I get back out.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The chest X-ray shows changes from emphysema and some collapse in the lower parts of your lungs—atelectasis. It’s not new, but it does make it harder to breathe.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So is it pneumonia again? Last time they gave me antibiotics.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You did get one dose of levofloxacin in the ER. But you’re not running a fever, and your white count is normal, so we don’t think it’s active pneumonia. The atelectasis is likely from not coughing deeply, maybe due to pain or fatigue.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve got pain from old injuries. Car wreck years ago. But I can manage it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We know you’ve had multiple fractures and a splenectomy. But right now, the main issues are the alcohol, your low blood pressure from dehydration, and your breathing.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I just want to go. I’ve been in the hospital too many times. I’ll be okay.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I understand. But you were agitated earlier and needed sedation with Haldol. You were also in restraints for safety. That means you weren’t fully in control.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I was confused, yeah. But I’m清醒 now. I know what I’m saying.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We were going to start a detox protocol and monitor you for withdrawal—given your history of seizures and DTs. Social work was also trying to file a Section 35 to help with involuntary hold, but the courts are closed today.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I don’t want that. I’m not staying. I understand the risks—you told me last time too.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes. I have to document that you’re leaving against medical advice. You’re alert now, and you say you understand—low blood pressure, breathing issues, risk of withdrawal.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I understand. I’m leaving. I’ll try to cut back on the drinking.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Okay. You’re able to walk and are not short of breath right now. But please consider going to a shelter or clinic tomorrow to check in.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll think about it. Thanks for the oxygen.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: James, I’m told you’re preparing to leave. Just confirming—you’re still making this choice?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes. I’m leaving. I feel better.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Alright. I’ve documented your condition as stable but leaving against medical advice. Please seek help if you start shaking, hallucinating, or can’t breathe.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. I don’t want to end up worse.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: James, you left the unit last night. We tried to reach you, but you were already gone. I’m glad you made it out safely, but I wish you’d stayed for detox.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I walked out because I didn’t want to be held. I’m not sick enough to stay.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your vitals were stable when you left, and you were alert. But your history puts you at high risk. Please follow up with someone—your primary care or a clinic.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll try. Thanks for the care.
